origin.description: Recompute the covariance of d at a new step size.

arguments.name: fracdiff.out
arguments.text: A fit from fracdiff. In Python the argument is fracdiff_out.

arguments.name: h
arguments.text: The finite-difference step. It is capped at 0.1.

origin.details: The second derivative uses trial log likelihoods whose variance divides by n - 1, while the maximized likelihood divides by n. The stored covariance is minus the reciprocal of that derivative.
origin.value: The standard error of d at the requested step.
origin.example: fit <- fracdiff(sin(1:40) + 0.3 * cos((1:40) / 3)); cat(fracdiff.var(sin(1:40) + 0.3 * cos((1:40) / 3), fit, h = 0.01)$stderror.dpq, "\n")

translation.description: Recompute the covariance of d at a new step size.

arguments.name: fracdiff.out
arguments.text: A fit from fracdiff. In Python the argument is fracdiff_out.

arguments.name: h
arguments.text: The finite-difference step. It is capped at 0.1.

translation.details: The second derivative uses trial log likelihoods whose variance divides by n - 1, while the maximized likelihood divides by n. The stored covariance is minus the reciprocal of that derivative.
translation.value: The standard error of d at the requested step.
translation.example: series = [math.sin(i) + 0.3 * math.cos(i / 3) for i in range(1, 41)]; fit = fracdiff(series); print(fracdiff_var(series, fit, 0.01).stderror_dpq[0])
